content:
Early in July, Apple added basic search functionality to its TestFlight app. You might think such a simple update would be universally welcome, but the same TestFlight update introduced a rather annoying bug for many users.

Personally, the bug had little impact on me. So initially I thought the TestFlight update was a simple yet meaningful improvement.

Sometimes, a small change can have a huge impact — especially for users with a large number of beta apps, and the latest TestFlight update is a perfect example. Apple has just updated TestFlight for iPhone, iPad, Mac and other platforms, with the new version 4.3 adding a "search bar for users to quickly find apps".

In hindsight, I did notice some strange behaviour, which I mentioned at the end of the article (although my understanding at the time was completely the opposite of what was actually happening):

The reason I didn't realise it was a bug is that for years I have kept all my installed TestFlight beta apps, for the purpose of "merging" my previously separate iCloud and App Store Apple accounts. It's not necessarily the most convenient method, but for me it was worth it.

Either way, this TestFlight bug did not escape the notice of MacStories' John Vorhees:

So you can imagine how excited I was when I saw Zac Hall's article about the new search bar in TestFlight over at 9to5Mac. I thought to myself, "At last!" So I immediately put aside what I was doing and went to update the app. [...] But unfortunately, there's a big "but" here. Previously, beta versions in TestFlight were sorted in reverse chronological order, which I personally really liked. [...] Now, expired betas and still-valid TestFlight betas are mixed together in alphabetical order, and the list of expired betas seems to have expanded to include every beta I've ever participated in. I did a rough count, and for me there are roughly 800 app entries. As you can imagine, only a very small number of those are actually still valid betas. The search function does help, but it's no longer possible to find things by scrolling.

By late August, John Gruber had written about the TestFlight update and this bug over at Daring Fireball:

Last night, more than a month after the bug appeared (and after Vorhees pointed it out), Apple finally updated TestFlight for the first time. Although the release notes only mention bug fixes, the update does indeed fix the bug in question.

TestFlight version 4.3.1 is a fix for users affected by this regression.
